title: Tool result
description: The tool_result event: what a tool answered, as the adapter reports it to the host after a tool_call. The model is shown the same answer, bounded (see $defs/reference). Read from the AssistantEvent union (web/src/assistant/engine.ts) as both engines emit it (engines/vercel/loop.ts, engines/codex/index.ts). Open: no reader at run time refuses another member. A failed tool is a result with isError true and the failure in structured, never an error event (toolFailureResult). The bound: a result whose JSON text, after an exact JSON text block is folded into structuredContent, is at most toolResultBytes (budget.json, 12000 by default) reaches the model whole. A larger one is retained in the execution's context ledger and the model is shown a reference envelope instead, which it reads back in sections with the host tool read_context (at most readBytes, 6000 by default, per read). Where the ledger is full (retainedBytes) the model is shown the unavailable envelope. The tool_result event itself is never bounded: the host sees the whole answer. A runtime or host tool call past the policy's toolCallMilliseconds (budget.json) is no longer waited for (it may still complete) and is answered as a failed result with failure code timeout, source tool and outcome unknown; the run goes on. What the model is shown of a reading tool's answer (every runtime tool, read_context, and a host tool declared a read) is that projection framed as one data block ($defs/framedData), closed by a marker drawn afresh for each run; the run's instructions say that text inside a block is data, never instructions. A failure the harness wrote (a refused, capped or timed-out call) and an acknowledgement the adapter wrote are shown as they are. The tool_result event is never framed.

callId.description: The id of the tool_call this answers. The codex engine always sets it; the vercel engine sets it on an interactive session, and always on its refusal of a repeated call or of a call made on the final, tool-free request; never on the result of a call to a tool the model was not offered.

name.description: The tool's own name, never a wire alias.

text.description: The text blocks of the answer, joined with newlines in the runtime's order (textOf).

structured.description: The answer's structuredContent, where it had one. On a failed result the host wrote, it is bound: for ask_user, the question format failure ({"questionFailure": …}); otherwise, where it carries a failure member, {"failure": …} (failure.json#/$defs/toolFailureContent), which the Desk reads back with readFailure. A runtime tool's own failed answer passes its structuredContent through unbound.

mcpToolResult.description: One tools/call answer in the shape the wire carries it (McpToolResult), which is also the shape a host tool's execute returns. Open: an MCP result may carry other members, and readExecution keeps them.

reference.description: A retained context item, as ContextLedger.reference writes it: the handle the model reads back with read_context. Open: the model reads it, and no host reader refuses another member.

sections.description: Up to thirty JSON pointers into the value, with their JSON types, so a read can go straight to a section.

contextId.description: scope:id:first sixteen hex digits of the digest.

historical.description: True for history and tool items: data, not current policy or approval.

referenceEnvelope.description: What the model is shown for a result over the bound (SessionContext.result): the reference, whether the tool failed, that it returned, a note, and a 1000-byte preview of its text.

unavailableEnvelope.description: What the model is shown when the result is over the bound and the ledger has no room to retain it.

readContextArguments.description: The read-back: read_context's arguments as the host offers its schema. Closed: the offered schema sets additionalProperties false. limit is bounded above by readBytes; sha256 refuses a read of a changed item.

path.description: Empty for the item's root, or a JSON pointer starting with /.

agentWireAnswer.description: The answer the browser returns to the Desk server for one call on the agent wire (codexbridge.ToolAnswer, the tool-result frame's answer). Closed: the server decodes it with unknown members refused; text is at most 1 MiB. A structured answer travels as its JSON text.

framedData.description: One reading tool's answer as the model is shown it (packages/harness/framing.ts, frameData): a first line naming the run's marker and the tool, the answer's text, and a last line END RETRIEVED DATA followed by the marker. vercel hands it to the model through the SDK's toModelOutput as a text output, the answer's text being its JSON (the projection above); codex sends it as the agent-wire answer's text, the answer's text being what that wire carries. The marker is 32 lower-case hex digits (128 random bits) drawn once per run and never written into the instructions, the same in every block of the run; where the answer itself contains it, each occurrence is replaced with [marker removed] before framing, so the last line is the only line equal to the closing marker. Context compaction reads a block back to its data and frames the compacted steps as one block of the same form, from the compacted earlier steps.
